sentences.text:
Government Of Nct Of Delhi vs M/S Beads Properties Pvt. Ltd.
on 7 August, 2023

Bench: C.T. Ravikumar, Sanjay Kumar
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Miscellaneous Application No.1622/2023
 in
 C.A. No.1522/2023
 Government Of Nct Of Delhi 
 Versus
 M/S Beads Properties Pvt. Ltd. 
 O R D E R
1. Heard learned counsel on both sides.
2. The applicant No.1 in the above mentioned Miscellaneous Application was the respondent in the captioned Civil Appeal.
It is true that despite being served, the respondent-therein/ applicant-herein has not chosen to enter appearance and contest the appeal.
Later, the Civil Appeal came to be disposed of as per judgment dated 13.03.2023.
The applicant now, prays for re-calling the judgment.
Normally, we will not be inclined to re-call such a judgment.
However, we think that the applicant has made out a case to persuade us to pass such an order.
3. Admittedly, the applicant-herein/ respondent-therein is a subsequent purchaser as relates the subject property.
Relying on the decisions of this Court in Siva Kumar v. Union of India & Ors.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v. Godfrey Phillip (I) Ltd. & Ors., Civil Appeal No.3073 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , it was held under the judgment sought to be recalled that a subsequent purchaser has no locus standi to challenge the acquisition or for seeking a declaration of lapsing of acquisition proceedings.

The applicant produced the common judgment dated 04.05.2017 in Civil Appeal No.6112/2017 and connected cases whereby and whereunder, the case filed against applicant No.1-herein viz. Civil Appeal No.6180/2017 arising out of SLP(C) No.8820/2016 by the Delhi Development Authority was also discussed.
Paragraphs 29 and 30 of the said judgment assume relevance while considering the right of the applicant as a subsequent purchaser.

They read thus:
29.

Thus, the subsequent purchaser, the assignee, the successor in interest, the power of attorney, etc., are compensation/land/owners/affected persons in terms of Government Of Nct Of Delhi vs M/S Beads Properties Pvt. Ltd. on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51846718/
1 the 2013 Act and such persons are entitled to file a case for a declaration that the land acquisition proceedings have lapsed by virtue of operation of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

entities.text: Government Of Nct Of Delhi vs M/S Beads Properties Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a declaration qua the land wherein indisputably they have an interest and they are affected by such acquisition.
For such a declaration, it cannot be said that the respondents/writ petitioners do not have any locus standi.
30. Thus, we do not find any merit in these appeals and they are accordingly dismissed.
All interlocutory Applications for impleadment and intervention, other than those by Legal Representatives, are also rejected.
Applications for impleadment of Legal Representatives are allowed.
There shall no order as to cost.
4. Admittedly, Delhi Development Authority was the 3 rd respondent in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023.

But the factum of dismissal of Civil Appeal No.6180/2017 arising from SLP(C) No.8820/2016 filed against the very same judgment under challenge in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023, was not specifically mentioned in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023.

Besides, while disposing of the Civil Appeal No.1522/2023, the fact that respondent No.1-therein/ the applicant No.1-herein, was a subsequent purchaser alone was considered in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023 and the right arising out of the judgment in Civil Appeal No.6180/2017, more particularly paragraphs 29 and 30, was not subsequently considered.

We shall not be understood to have held that the petitioner-herein got an indefeasible right solely on the ground of being subsequent purchaser of the subject property to challenge the acquisition/ to seek for declaration of lapsing by virtue of the aforesaid decision and certainly, it is a matter to be looked into in the light of the dictum laid down in the said judgment as also other relevant decisions, in view of the factual position obtained.

Since none of the questions was considered and the decision was rendered taking into account the status of the applicant as subsequent purchaser only, we are of the view that it is a case where this Court should invoke power to recall the order passed in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023 so as to have a judgment considering all relevant aspects.
In that view of the matter, the judgment passed in Civil Appeal No.1522/2023 stands recalled.
The case stands restored into its original number.
5. The I.A. No.83509/2023 is allowed and the M.A. is disposed of accordingly.

6. List the matter(s) along with M.A. D.No.32257/2021 for further consideration.
.....................,J.
(C.T. RAVIKUMAR) .....................,J.
(SANJAY KUMAR)
NEW DELHI;
7TH AUGUST, 2023.
